sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for tool types
sections.what: Brings in the icon type and the React type, which the tool contract refers to.
sections.why: Needed so the contract can name the icon and the page component types.

sections.name: ToolDef
sections.title: Required tool fields
sections.what: Lists the fields every tool must provide: a unique slug, name, subtitle, status (live or coming soon), icon, path and page component.
sections.why: The comments say a single shape lets every tool be added without editing the app's routes.
sections.watch_out: The comments point to client/src paths, which do not match this project's layout, so they may be out of date.

sections.name: isToolDef
sections.title: Runtime shape check
sections.what: Checks an unknown object at run time to confirm it has the required fields with valid values, including a path that starts with a slash.
sections.why: Likely reason: types are removed when the app is built, so a run-time check is needed for data that arrives from outside the type system.
sections.watch_out: It is not called in the registry shown here, so it currently does nothing in the visible code.

summary: Defines the required shape of every tool module, and a check that confirms an unknown object has that shape.
purpose: Gives all tools one shared contract, so the registry can treat them the same way.
why: The comments say the registry collects tools automatically, so every tool must provide the same fields.
how: The tool type lists the required fields: slug, name, subtitle, status, icon, path and component. The check function looks at an unknown object and confirms each required field is present and valid.
inputs: Any unknown object, for the check. Compile-time type information for the tool shape.
outputs: A yes or no answer from the check, and a type that tools must match.
risks: The comments give paths under client/src, but this project keeps tools under artifacts/capital-projects/src, so those comments look out of date. The check function is not called in the registry file shown here, so it has no effect on the visible code.
debug: If a tool is rejected, compare its fields with the tool type, and confirm its path starts with a slash. Check whether the registry actually calls the check function.
